channel.title: Money Matters Daily — Pinterest Feed (Building Credit)
channel.description: Curated, approved pins for the "Building Credit" board. Not the main site feed.

item.title: Does Checking Your Own Credit Score Hurt It? Soft vs. Hard Inquiries Explained
item.description: Checking your own credit never lowers your score, but applying for credit can. Here's the difference between soft and hard inquiries, which checks count as which, how long a hard inquiry matters, and how to shop for a loan without piling up damage.

item.title: Secured Credit Cards Explained: How They Work and When to Graduate Off One
item.description: A secured credit card is a regular card backed by a refundable deposit, and it's one of the most reliable ways to build or rebuild credit. Here's how the deposit works, what to look for, how to use the card, and how to know when it's time to move on.

item.title: How to Dispute an Error on Your Credit Report (Step by Step)
item.description: Credit report errors are common, and fixing them is free. Here's how to find a mistake, dispute it with both the credit bureau and the company that reported it, what the 30-day clock means, and what to do if the answer is no.

item.title: How UK Credit Scores Work: Experian vs Equifax vs TransUnion
item.description: The UK doesn't have one credit score — it has three, on three different scales, and two of them just changed. Here's what Experian, Equifax, and TransUnion actually measure, their current bands, and why the same financial history produces three different numbers.

item.title: Credit Utilization Explained: The Number That Moves Your Score Fastest
item.description: Credit utilization is 30% of your FICO score and resets every billing cycle, making it the fastest lever you have. Here's how it's actually calculated — per-card, overall, and by statement date — with worked examples.

item.title: What Actually Hurts Your Credit Score (and What's Just a Myth)
item.description: Credit scores run on a weighted formula, not intuition — and some of the most common 'credit tips' people follow are myths that do nothing or actively backfire. Here's what really moves the number, ranked by weight.

item.title: How to Build Credit From Scratch (When You Have None)
item.description: No credit history isn't the same as bad credit, but it creates the same problem: nobody will lend to you yet. Here's the actual order of operations.
